_doc: Capability taxonomy for the card-text-driven tech-matchup detector. Each capability tag describes an effect a card has based on its rules text. Extracted by patterns in card_capability_patterns.json and matched against opposing-side tags by card_capability_interactions.json.

attack.ignores_effects.desc: Attack damage is not affected by any effects on the defending Pokemon. Bypasses damage-reduction abilities, KO-prevention abilities, EX-immunity, and bench-protection on the active. Example: Mega Lopunny ex (PFL 84) Spiky Hopper.

attack.bench_damage.desc: Attack deals damage to one or more Benched Pokemon. Bypasses front-line bulk and pressures multi-prize backline targets. Example: Drayton (DRI 21) Dynamic Lightning, Charizard ex Burning Darkness.

attack.weakness_bypass.desc: Attack damage is dealt regardless of Weakness — neutralises type-disadvantaged matchups where the opponent would otherwise be a hard counter.

ability.ko_prevention.desc: Survives a lethal attack with 1+ HP remaining when at full HP. Example: Crustle (BLK 130) Sturdy: 'If this Pokemon has full HP and would be Knocked Out by damage from an attack, it is not Knocked Out, and its remaining HP becomes 10.'

ability.ex_immunity.desc: Takes zero damage from Pokemon ex / Pokemon-EX attacks. Hard-walls every ex-attacker unless bypassed. Example: Cornerstone Mask Ogerpon variants.

ability.bench_protection.desc: Prevents damage done to Benched Pokemon. Examples: Manaphy (Wave Veil), Mr. Mime, Jirachi-style protection.

ability.damage_reduction.desc: Reduces incoming damage by a fixed amount (e.g. '-30 damage from attacks'). Eats away at attacker math but doesn't fully prevent KO.

ability.bench_search.desc: Searches the deck for a specific category of Pokemon and benches them, accelerating board setup.

ability.gust_effect.desc: Switches one of the opponent's Benched Pokemon to the Active Spot. Critical for picking off support pieces or punishing setup Pokemon.

disruption.hand_reset.desc: Forces the opponent to shuffle their hand and draw a different (usually smaller) number of cards. Examples: Iono, N, Roxanne.
